title: Roman shipwreck with 500 amphorae found off coast of Sicily

paragraphs.en: A 2,100-year-old Roman shipwreck carrying about 500 amphorae has been discovered 3 miles off the coast of Mazara del Vallo in Sicily.
paragraphs.zh: 在距西西里马扎拉德尔瓦洛海岸3英里处，发现了一艘载有约500只双耳陶瓶的、有着2100年历史的罗马沉船。

paragraphs.en: Italy’s Carabinieri cultural heritage protection squad investigated the wreck with the help of divers and underwater cameras after receiving a tip-off from fishers. The vessel was found at a depth of about 46 metres (151ft) and was carrying hundreds of amphorae – ancient two-handled ceramic jars with a narrow neck – thought to have been used mainly to transport wine.
paragraphs.zh: 意大利宪兵队文化遗产保护分队在收到渔民的线报后，借助潜水员和水下摄像机的帮助调查了这艘沉船。该船被发现于约46米（151英尺）深的水下，载有数百只双耳陶瓶——带有窄颈、双耳柄的古代陶罐，据认为主要被用来运输葡萄酒。

paragraphs.en: The wreck, measuring about 21 metres long and 6 metres wide, was described by Italy’s culture minister, Alessandro Giuli, as “one of the most important underwater archaeological discoveries of recent years”.
paragraphs.zh: 这艘沉船长约21米、宽约6米，被意大利文化部长亚历山德罗·朱利形容为“近年来最重要的水下考古发现之一”。

paragraphs.en: Giuli said the wreck offered “precious fragments of our history” and provided further evidence of the trade routes and exchanges that made the Mediterranean “a crossroads of civilisations”.
paragraphs.zh: 朱利说，这艘沉船提供了“我们历史中珍贵的碎片”，并进一步印证了那些使地中海成为“文明交汇处”的贸易路线和交流往来。

paragraphs.en: The divers Giacomo De Mola and Igor Bisulli described how they came across the wreck.
paragraphs.zh: 潜水员贾科莫·德莫拉和伊戈尔·比苏利描述了他们是怎样偶然发现这艘沉船的。

paragraphs.en: “Visibility wasn’t the best … I got closer. And my heart stopped. Below me was a vast expanse of amphorae,” De Mola said in an Instagram post accompanying video footage of the discovery.
paragraphs.zh: “能见度不是最好……我靠近了一些。我的心跳停了一拍。在我脚下是一片辽阔的双耳陶瓶。”德莫拉在Instagram上发布帖子并附上发现过程的视频片段时写道。

paragraphs.en: “This is, without a doubt, the most incredible discovery of my life,” he said. “It’s hard to describe what it feels like to be among the first humans, in nearly 20 centuries, to see that place again.”
paragraphs.zh: “这无疑是我一生中最不可思议的发现。”他说，“作为近20个世纪里第一批再次看到那个地方的人类，那种感觉难以言表。”

paragraphs.en: Most of the ship’s cargo consisted of Dressel 1A amphorae, widely used to transport wine and particularly valuable to archaeologists because they can help reconstruct the commercial networks that linked Italy with other parts of the Mediterranean between the second and first centuries BC.
paragraphs.zh: 沉船的大部分货物由Dressel 1A型双耳陶瓶组成，这种陶瓶被广泛用于运输葡萄酒，对考古学家尤其珍贵，因为它们有助于还原公元前二世纪至一世纪之间连接意大利与地中海其他地区的商业网络。
